# Automate AI-Powered Instagram Reels & YouTube Shorts Creation and Publishing

## Quick overview
Create AI-assisted narrated vertical videos through a companion studio and renderer, then coordinate Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts delivery. The studio, renderer and SSH media helper are external dependencies.

## How it works
Reserve a job/budget, generate and review copy, poll rendering, preserve the original MP4, complete Instagram publication, then upload and verify the preserved video on YouTube.

## Setup
1. Keep this template inactive while configuring it.
2. Assign your own credentials; remove inherited account associations before sharing.
3. Install the matching external runtime and persistent storage. The JSON does not include these services.
4. Configure service URLs, helper paths, HTTPS media routes and target accounts.
5. Use fictional sample content, neutral colors and assets you own; inspect the rendered output for unwanted branding.
6. Prove preview/no-publishing behavior before authorizing any live platform test.

## Customization
Change content, layouts, schedules and timezone in their actual configuration locations. Keep authorization, validation and receipts intact.

## Publishing safety
Manual execution can reach real platform writes. Do not rely on a trigger name, dryRun flag or YouTube privateTest without validating its actual branch/backend behavior. This note does not certify runtime readiness.

## Documentation
[Setup, testing and operations](https://paoloronco.notion.site/Automate-AI-Powered-Instagram-Reels-YouTube-Shorts-Creation-and-Publishing-41af0ba27c32817490eeff675e958ce2)

## 1. Reserve brief and budget
Manual, scheduled and authenticated test inputs share the production path. Reserve before paid calls and inspect canGenerate plus the service response.

The backend enforces budgets and job reuse. Execution-derived keys alone do not deduplicate separate executions. A test trigger name does not prevent posting.

## 2. Write, review and render
Validate writer output, facts, novelty and provider usage. The companion service must enforce the intended correction limit and reviewer decision.

Poll until ready; stop on failed/rejected states. Inspect output and licensing manually. AI review is not proof of factual accuracy; previews can incur API costs.

## 3. Gated Instagram publication
Keep previews when publishing is disabled or previewOnly is true. Otherwise claim an action, use your Meta OAuth account and persist the sanitized result before continuing.

Real success needs a persisted media ID/permalink. Verify dry-run behavior in the backend. Reconcile uncertain writes before retrying; do not assume claims guarantee exactly-once delivery.

## 4. Authorized asset delivery
Validate job/file and envelope shape, then let the studio verify signature, expiry and exact asset authorization. Return only the requested bytes or unavailable.

Expose the required HTTPS media route, not internal job/admin APIs. Test expired/tampered links; keep secrets and live signed URLs out of screenshots and exports.

## 5. Preserve and upload the original MP4
Preserve the matching job's original media before Instagram publication. The YouTube path follows the Instagram receipt; validate the authenticated channel, claim media and persist a returned video ID immediately.

Verify helper dry-run behavior. A privateTest upload changes YouTube visibility only; it does not make a preceding Instagram post private.

## 6. Verify YouTube and recover safely
Check video/channel identity, processing, dimensions, audio-stream metadata and duration when file details are available. Listen to the original MP4 separately.

Retain pending video IDs and finalize the receipt only after verification. Resume incomplete stages instead of reuploading or reposting Instagram. Platform classification and visibility are not guaranteed by local checks.
